answers.question: What does my plan look like over the next few months?
answers.text:
Your long-term plan spans 12 weeks across 8 phases, running from Monday, August 31 to Sunday, November 22. You are currently in the Base phase, which runs through Sunday, September 13. The next phase starts on Monday, September 14.

The phases are:

- Base: Monday, August 31 to Sunday, September 13 (2 weeks). You start the return to a comfortable 5K by reintroducing short jog-and-walk efforts that keep your knee comfortable.
- Build: Monday, September 14 to Sunday, September 20 (1 week). Your focus shifts to linking the easy jog portions seamlessly while keeping the effort controlled.
- Recovery: Monday, September 21 to Sunday, September 27 (1 week). A quieter week lets your knee and energy systems absorb the new routine.
- Base: Monday, September 28 to Sunday, October 4 (1 week). You return to consistent jog-walk work with refreshed legs and a calm pace.
- Build: Monday, October 5 to Sunday, October 18 (2 weeks). You extend your comfortable running stretches and make steady jogging feel more automatic.
- Recovery: Monday, October 19 to Sunday, October 25 (1 week). You ease back with gentle walking and short easy outings so your body can consolidate.
- Build: Monday, October 26 to Sunday, November 8 (2 weeks). You rebuild consistency with run/walk sessions that support the goal without overloading the knee.
- Maintain: Monday, November 9 to Sunday, November 22 (2 weeks). You preserve the aerobic base you have built and keep the routine sustainable.

And here is the week-by-week breakdown:

- Week 1, starting Monday, August 31 (Base): key session Run/walk (run). You start the return to a comfortable 5K by reintroducing short jog-and-walk efforts that keep your knee comfortable.
- Week 2, starting Monday, September 7 (Base): key session Run/walk (run). You establish a repeatable walk-jog routine so your right knee adapts to regular movement.
- Week 3, starting Monday, September 14 (Build): key session Easy (run). Your focus shifts to linking the easy jog portions seamlessly while keeping the effort controlled.
- Week 4, starting Monday, September 21 (Recovery): key session Recovery (walk). A quieter week lets your knee and energy systems absorb the new routine.
- Week 5, starting Monday, September 28 (Base): key session Run/walk (run). You return to consistent jog-walk work with refreshed legs and a calm pace.
- Week 6, starting Monday, October 5 (Build): key session Easy (run). You extend your comfortable running stretches and make steady jogging feel more automatic.
- Week 7, starting Monday, October 12 (Build): key session Long (run). Endurance becomes the priority as you spend more time in a relaxed run rhythm.
- Week 8, starting Monday, October 19 (Recovery): key session Recovery (walk). You ease back with gentle walking and short easy outings so your body can consolidate.
- Week 9, starting Monday, October 26 (Build): key session Run/walk (run). You rebuild consistency with run/walk sessions that support the goal without overloading the knee.
- Week 10, starting Monday, November 2 (Build): key session Easy (run). The focus turns to maintaining a steady running rhythm for longer stretches.
- Week 11, starting Monday, November 9 (Maintain): key session Easy (run). You preserve the aerobic base you have built and keep the routine sustainable.
- Week 12, starting Monday, November 16 (Maintain): key session Easy (run). A stable closing week locks in the habits that move you toward a comfortable 5K.

That gives you the full picture of the coming months.
